findings.message: An unreadable config.yaml (missing, permission error) returns [] and is treated as 'no presets configured'. The build then proceeds with only base and exits 0, so 'could not read config' reads as 'nothing configured'. Distinguish the missing/unreadable case: warn on stderr and exit non-zero (or at least exit 1).
findings.scenario: specclaw-presets /wrong/dir (or a config.yaml with mode 000) -> prints only base.md, exit 0; build silently skips python/dotnet presets the user configured.

findings.message: The parser only understands the inline `[..]` and block-list forms. Any other shape (e.g. `presets: python` scalar, `presets: []` mixed with comments, CRLF line endings, `presets:  # comment` followed by a list, or a `presets:` key nested under another section) silently yields [] and exit 0 instead of flagging a malformed value. Fail closed: if a `presets:` key is present but no form matched, warn and exit 1.
findings.scenario: config.yaml has `presets: python` or `presets: [python] # stack` handled? The first fits the regex only partly: `presets: python` matches neither pattern -> returns [], prints only base.md, exit 0; the python preset is silently dropped.

findings.message: `Extends:` is matched only when the file's first non-blank line is exactly that; the README and header comment say 'start the file with Extends', but a `Extends: x` with trailing text, in different case, or after a `# Preset:` title line is silently ignored and the local file replaces the built-in with no warning. Also `Extends: <other>` where <other> is neither local nor built-in yields (parent, None), reported unknown, but a local preset extending a name that itself extends is silently single-level. Additionally the extends() open() has no error handling (non-UTF-8 file raises a traceback, exit 1 with no 'unknown preset' message).
findings.scenario: local dotnet.md begins `# Preset: dotnet (ours)` then `Extends: dotnet` on line 2 -> treated as a full replacement; the built-in dotnet rules are silently dropped, no warning. A local preset with invalid UTF-8 bytes -> Python UnicodeDecodeError traceback instead of a clean message.

findings.message: Tests cover only the inline `[..]` config form. The block-list parser branch, `Extends: other-name` (non-self), local-extends-local, dedupe, missing config, and the Extends-not-first-line case have no tests, so the variants of this resolver are unproven. Also AC-5 only checks the exit code with the `../x` name; it does not verify that no file outside presets/ is read.
findings.scenario: Break the block-list regex (e.g. delete that branch) -> every test stays green, yet `presets:\n  - python` configs resolve to base only.

findings.message: AC-6 asserts $TMP/n/.specclaw/presets/README.md exists but the diff never creates $TMP/n in the added lines; it depends on an earlier fixture elsewhere in the file. If that fixture does not run specclaw-init, the check is vacuous or fails for the wrong reason, and it does not verify init content matches the template.
findings.scenario: If $TMP/n is produced by a different fixture that does not call specclaw-init, AC-6 fails (or passes against stale state) regardless of the init change.

findings.message: builtin() and local() are two copies of the same lookup differing only in the base directory, and the name regex is applied in each; the config parsing is also a hand-rolled YAML parser while other specclaw scripts have their own parsers. Merge into one helper taking a directory.
findings.scenario: A later fix to name validation in one helper (e.g. allowing underscores) and not the other lets local and built-in lookups disagree.

findings.message: Unknown preset name from config.yaml is echoed to stderr unsanitised, and realpath is used without verifying the resolved path stays inside presets/ (a symlinked <name>.md pointing elsewhere is followed and its contents handed to the agent as instructions).
findings.scenario: A repo-committed .specclaw/presets/x.md symlink to ~/.ssh/config, with `presets: [x]` -> build reads that file into context.
